chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), on the days he fasted, would order a sheep to be slaughtered and cut into pieces and cooked.
Then when evening came, he would lean over the cooking pots until he could smell the aroma of the broth — while he was fasting.
Then he would say: 'Bring the bowls; fill them for the family of so-and-so, and fill them for the family of so-and-so.'
Then he would be brought bread and dates, and that would be his dinner.
May God bless him and his forefathers.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin do with food on his fasting days?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the extraordinary practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, as) during his fasts: he would cook meat and distribute it to the poor and neighbors, while himself breaking his fast only with bread and dates. The account highlights the Imam's simultaneous restraint and generosity — he denied himself the food he had cooked entirely for others, enduring the temptation of its aroma while fasting. This conduct exemplifies the Shia ethical ideal of feeding others at the expense of one's own comfort, echoing the Quranic praise for those who feed the poor despite their own need (76:8).
